description_full: Pegasystems Inc. develops, markets, licenses, hosts, and supports enterprise software in the United States, rest of the Americas, the United Kingdom, rest of Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia-Pacific. It provides Pega Infinity, a software portfolio comprising of Pega Customer Decision Hub, a real-time AI-powered decision engine, which can predict a customer's behavior and recommend the next best action to take across channels in real-time; Pega Customer Service to anticipate customer needs, connect customers to people and systems, and automate customer interactions to evolve the customer service experience, as well as to allow enterprises to deliver interactions across channels and enhance employee productivity; and Pega Platform, a software for AI-powered workflow automation for increasing the efficiency of clients' processes and operational workflows. The company also offers Situational Layer Cake that organizes logic into layers that map to the unique dimensions of a client's business, such as customer types, lines of business, geographies, etc.; Pega GenAI Blueprint to rapidly prototype and accelerate the development and deployment of applications; Pega Cloud that allows clients to develop, test, and deploy applications; Pega Catalyst, which helps clients to transform and prototype their customer journeys; Pega Academy, which offers enablement content for Pega product implementations, such as instructor-led and online training to its employees, clients, and partners; and global service assurance and client support services. It primarily markets its software and services to financial services, healthcare, communications and media, government, insurance, manufacturing and high tech, and consumer industries through a direct sales force, as well as partnerships with technology providers and application developers. Pegasystems Inc. was incorporated in 1983 and is headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts.

financial_summary: Pegasystems Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $4.5B market cap on $1.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at -20% against a 12% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 69% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $491M in free cash flow — roughly 28 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.28× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 11.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 48% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 30% over the past year excluding the latest month.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $13.03 (margin of safety -109%), so there is no valuation cushion.

The 7 covering analysts target $41.00 on average, 50% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 20% falls short of the cost of capital of 11.6%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 3.44).
It runs a 69% gross margin and converts 28% of revenue into free cash flow, or 19% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.28x.
ROE of 50% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.1x equity multiplier).

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $425.8M (10% of market cap).

growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.8% over 3 years, 11.4% over 5 years and 9.8% over 10 years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.26 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 1.2x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 22%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.1x, 0.8% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 31, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.

own: Insiders own 48.0%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 57%.
